recipes.title: Chicken Adobo
recipes.dish_alt: Glossy braised chicken adobo thighs with rice and broccoli
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Braising in Soy, Vinegar & Bay Leaf
recipes.prep_alt: Chicken and pork braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, and bay leaf for adobo

sections.heading: Steps
items: Marinate the chicken in soy sauce and garlic 15-30 minutes.
Sear the chicken skin-side down in oil 3-4 minutes per side until golden.
Add the reserved marinade, vinegar, water, bay leaves, peppercorns, and sugar.
Boil uncovered without stirring 3 minutes to cook off the vinegar's raw sharpness.
Cover, reduce to a simmer, and cook 25-30 minutes until the chicken is fork-tender.
Uncover and simmer 5-8 more minutes until the sauce reduces to a glossy glaze.
Taste and adjust the salty-sour-sweet balance.
Serve hot over steamed rice, spooning the glaze over the top.

recipes.title: Pork Sinigang (Sour Tamarind Soup)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of pork sinigang with vegetables in a sour tamarind broth
recipes.prep_alt: Radish, cabbage, corn, garlic, and onion prepped for pork sinigang

sections.heading: Steps
items: Boil the pork with onion and tomato, skimming foam, then simmer 40-45 minutes until tender.
Stir in the tamarind soup base until dissolved and the broth turns sour.
Add the radish and eggplant, simmer 5 minutes.
Add the string beans and chili, simmer 3-4 minutes more.
Season with fish sauce to taste.
Stir in the kangkong or spinach last and cook 1 minute until just wilted.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with rice, extra fish sauce, and calamansi.

recipes.title: Pancit Canton (Stir-Fried Noodles)
recipes.dish_alt: Pancit canton noodles stir-fried with shrimp, pork, carrots, and snow peas
recipes.prep_label: Prep — A Tray of Freshly Tossed Noodles
recipes.prep_alt: A catering tray of pancit canton noodles tossed with vegetables and pork

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the dried noodles in warm water 5-10 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Sauté the garlic and onion 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the pork, cook until no longer pink, then add shrimp and cook until opaque.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and oyster sauce, and bring to a simmer.
Add the carrot, then the cabbage and snow peas, cooking until crisp-tender.
Add the drained noodles and toss 3-5 minutes until they absorb the liquid.
Season with black pepper to taste.
Serve hot with calamansi or lime wedges squeezed over the top.

recipes.title: Chicken Tinola
recipes.dish_alt: Chicken tinola soup with chayote and malunggay leaves in a light ginger broth
recipes.prep_alt: Raw chicken, chayote, chilies, garlic, and onion prepped for chicken tinola

sections.heading: Steps
items: Sauté the ginger 1-2 minutes, then add the garlic and onion and cook 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until lightly browned.
Pour in the fish sauce, then add the water or broth.
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered partway 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the green papaya or chayote and simmer 5-8 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the malunggay or spinach and simmer 1-2 minutes until wilted.
Taste and add more fish sauce if needed.
Serve hot in bowls with steamed rice alongside.

recipes.title: Bicol Express (Spicy Pork in Coconut Milk)
recipes.dish_alt: Bicol Express pork simmered in coconut milk with sliced green chilies
recipes.prep_alt: Sautéed shrimp paste, the key flavor base for Bicol Express

sections.heading: Steps
items: Sauté the garlic, onion, and ginger 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook 4-5 minutes until lightly browned at the edges.
Stir in the shrimp paste and cook 1 minute until it darkens and smells toasty.
Pour in the coconut milk, stirring to combine.
Simmer gently, uncovered, 25-30 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce thickens.
Add the long green chilies and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the Thai chilies for the final 2 minutes, to taste.
Serve over steamed rice.

recipes.title: Beef Caldereta
recipes.dish_alt: Beef Caldereta stew with potato and carrot in a rich tomato-liver-spread sauce
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Liver Spread, the Signature Ingredient
recipes.prep_alt: A can of liver spread, the ingredient that gives Caldereta its rich sauce

sections.heading: Steps
items: Brown the beef in batches, 3-4 minutes per side, then set aside.
Sauté the onion and garlic 2-3 minutes until softened.
Return the beef to the pot with tomato sauce, broth, and bay leaf; bring to a boil.
Cover partway and simmer 60-75 minutes until the beef is fork-tender.
Add the potato and carrot, simmer 10-12 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the liver spread until it dissolves and thickens the sauce.
Add the bell peppers and simmer 5 minutes until just softened.
Stir in the shredded cheese, if using, until melted.
Season with salt and serve hot over steamed rice.

recipes.title: Lumpia Shanghai (Fried Spring Rolls)
recipes.dish_alt: Crispy fried lumpia Shanghai spring rolls with a sweet dipping sauce
recipes.prep_alt: A plate piled high with freshly fried, hand-rolled lumpia Shanghai

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Sweet chili sauce or banana ketchup

sections.heading: Steps
items: Mix the ground pork, carrot, green onion, garlic, soy sauce, salt, and pepper until slightly sticky.
Spoon a log of filling near the bottom corner of a wrapper laid in a diamond orientation.
Fold the bottom corner over the filling, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Seal the top corner with a dab of beaten egg. Repeat with remaining wrappers.
Heat the oil to about 175°C (350°F).
Fry the rolls in batches, turning occasionally, 4-5 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels or a wire rack.
Serve hot over rice with sweet chili sauce or banana ketchup for dipping.

recipes.title: Leche Flan (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Sliced leche flan showing its caramel top and dense custard, pooled in caramel sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Leche flan sliced into wedges, showing the dense custard and caramel layer

sections.heading: Steps
items: Melt the sugar with water in a llanera or small mold until deep amber, then swirl to coat the bottom.
Whisk the egg yolks gently, just enough to break them up.
Stir in the condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla, and zest until smooth.
Strain the mixture into the mold over the hardened caramel.
Cover the mold tightly with foil.
Steam over gently simmering water 25-30 minutes until set but still slightly jiggly.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Unmold onto a plate so the caramel pools over the custard, then slice and serve chilled.
